1.explanation: In this stand-alone React demo we simulate loading of the webhook URL. Before the URL is fetched, we render a <CodeSnippet disabled> expecting it to grey out and disable both the copy button and keyboard focus – however Carbon’s CodeSnippet component currently ignores the disabled prop. You can tab into the copy icon and activate it, even though no URL is shown. This reproduces the accessibility issue described in the bug report. In your live code you can swap in CodeSnippetSkeleton or roll your own CSS, but neither gives you a fully ‘disabled’ snippet with correct keyboard behavior, which is why the feature request for a built-in disabled state is needed.
1.bug_scenario: On a form where we need to display a code snippet placeholder before the real value is available (in this case a WhatsApp webhook URL), we’d like to render our CodeSnippet in a ‘disabled’ state: greyed-out text, copy button hidden or at least not keyboard focusable. Currently Carbon’s CodeSnippet component does not support a disabled prop or state. If you try to pass disabled={true}, nothing changes – the snippet still looks active and you can tab to and click the copy button even though no real value is shown. This is an accessibility problem because keyboard users can focus and activate the copy button on an empty or placeholder snippet.
